info.title: ControlServer.FakeOnboard
info.description: A synthetic Onboard peer. It connects out to ControlServer over the NDJSON protocol, completes the five-step recovery handshake (ADR-cross-0029), heartbeats every two seconds, and answers business requests according to a policy a scenario can change while the session is live. This HTTP surface is the control plane only; the protocol traffic is a TCP connection to ControlServer.

get.summary: Liveness. status is "live" only once the server has granted READY.
Session generation, readiness, safety state, policy, open requests and the wire log.
get.description: readiness is DISCONNECTED before the handshake and after the peer loses the socket, READY once the server grants it, and FAULTED when the read pump died -- readinessReasonCode then carries the exception. pending lists requests the peer is holding open, keyed the way /answer names them. wire is the last 200 messages in either direction, a diagnostic rather than asserted state, so it does not move the revision.

put.summary: Sets how the peer answers each kind of request.
put.description: Auto answers as a working vehicle would, as soon as the request arrives. Manual holds it open for /answer. Silent never answers -- which is what a station operation running out its own operator timeout looks like from the server's side.

put.summary: Reports a new abstract safety state, sending SafetyStateChanged.
put.description: This is how a scenario makes the vehicle move and stop as Onboard sees it, which is the half the RIoT double cannot express. safetyStateVersion defaults to the next one; pin it to exercise a revision the server refuses. Fields not given keep their current value.

409.description: RUN_ID_MISMATCH, COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT, REVISION_CONFLICT, or NOT_ALLOWED_IN_STATE when no session is connected.

put.summary: Answers one request the peer is holding open under Manual policy.
put.description: The answer is remembered verbatim: ControlServer replays an unsettled command on every poll, and ADR-cross-0006 requires the peer to return its existing result rather than a new one. A second OperationResult under the same slotOperationAttemptId with a fresh resultId is a content conflict the server tears the session down over.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: "sublot", "safety-check", "operation:{slotOperationAttemptId}", or "activation:{activationId}". Read the exact keys from /control/v1/snapshot.

409.description: NOT_FOUND when no request is open under that key, NOT_ALLOWED_IN_STATE when no session is connected.

put.summary: Answers a held load command with a determinate failure (ADR-cross-0058 decision 5).
put.description: The first target slot FAILED under reasonCode, the rest NOT_STARTED, every slot EMPTY, LOCKED and RESET. The v2 onboard does not send this; the server settles it defensively, and only after the station departure deadline. Remembered verbatim like /answer, so a replayed command gets the same result back. This peer has no deadline of its own: the scenario decides when to send it.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: "operation:{slotOperationAttemptId}" of a held LOAD command. Read the exact key from /control/v1/snapshot.

400.description: INVALID_ARGUMENT when the request under that key is not a LOAD SlotOperationCommand.

409.description: NOT_FOUND when no request is open under that key, NOT_ALLOWED_IN_STATE when no session is connected.

put.summary: Drops the session to ControlServer (connected: false) or opens a new one with a full handshake (connected: true).
put.description: Not routed through the command engine. A reconnect the server refuses answers 409 CONNECTION_CHANGE_FAILED with the reason in detail.

200.description: connected, changed, sessionGeneration and readiness after the change.

put.summary: Replaces the whole alarm set and publishes it as the next OnboardAlarmSnapshot.
put.description: alarmSnapshotRevision moves on by one. A disconnected peer keeps the set and reports it in its next handshake.

400.description: INVALID_ARGUMENT: an alarm without code or subjectType, or a severity other than INFO, WARNING or CRITICAL.

get.summary: Every load cancellation this peer raised: the request, the server's decision and authorized slots, and the result it reported and whether the server acknowledged it.
get.description: Kept outside the command engine; reading it does not move the revision.

put.summary: Raises LoadCancellationStartRequested under cancellationId, the way the operator's load cancellation does.
put.description: slotOperationAttemptId null is the cancellation before any sublot entry. On AUTHORIZED with no slots the peer reports LoadCancellationResult ALL_EMPTY with no slot results at once; an authorization naming slots is recorded and left unanswered, because this peer has no slot IO to prove them empty. Not routed through the command engine.

200.description: cancellationId and the requestMessageId it went out under.

400.description: INVALID_ARGUMENT: an id is not a UUID.

409.description: NOT_ALLOWED_IN_STATE: no session to ControlServer is open.

completed.description: true for a completed operation, a SAFE pre-departure answer or an accepted activation; false for a failed one or a fingerprint-mismatch rejection. Ignored for a sublot submission.

deliver.description: Activations only. false concludes the activation on the peer but holds its result back until ControlServer replays the command after a reconnect.

reasonCode.description: The failed slot's reason code. OPERATOR_TIMEOUT is the only one protocol 2.0.0 allows on an OperationResult; any other goes to recovery on the server.
